title: Arming the Brothers for Spiritual Combat
english: A cowardly soldier makes the hands of warriors go slack, and a careless monk drains the eagerness of his brothers. A swarm of bees produces a honeycomb, and a community of brothers produces the kingdom of heaven. A trumpet rouses the eagerness of warriors, and teaching in active virtue rouses the zeal of disciples. Arm your brothers, leader, with words [the Greek here is corrupt: "of fingers"], and put on them the breastplate of the promises of good things to come. Fence them with the shield of faith in struggles, and put greaves on them with hope in God. Shoe their feet [the printed verb is corrupt; "shoe" is a conjecture] with the lessons of the gospel, and gird their loins with words of self-control. Put into their hand the sharpest anger as a sword against the passions, and set a phalanx of the passions against pleasure.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG De magistris et discipulis u01-rem-early
orientation: Evagrius continues his direct address to the monastic leader, now commanding him to equip his brothers with spiritual armor and weapons for the fight against the passions.

title: Training, praise, and correction without anger
english: Train your soldiers in their thoughts, so that they are skilled for battle, and make defeat a fearful thing by the warning of eternal punishment. Proclaim the victor with shining praises, for praise also knows how to make people more zealous. And heal the one who has been wounded with compassion, for forgiveness shames the sensible person no less than a warning does. Do not be moved to anger against a disciple who has sinned, for it is not holy to wound your own soul before healing another. Instead, correct him patiently toward the good. For a physician heals the disease and does not grow angry with the one who has fallen ill involuntarily. When a physician cuts, he does it without anger; and when a teacher corrects, let him not mix anger into the correction.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG De magistris et discipulis u01-rem-mid
orientation: Evagrius is addressing the monastic leader directly, continuing his instructions on how to equip and guide disciples in spiritual combat.

title: The desert journey to Elim as the path to freedom from passions
english: Guide those who are fleeing the land of Egypt through the desert, for scarcity knows how to train people in self-control, even those who are just beginning in virtue. Encamp at Elim—its gates are interpreted as a symbol of the entrance that leads to virtue—and point out the seventy palm trees. Encamp also by the twelve springs, for the palm trees must proclaim victory to you as a symbol, and the springs must cool the flame of the passions by providing streams abundantly. Do this until they have destroyed all the foreign nations and arrive at the promised land, where they will live the blessed life of freedom from passions, receiving true joy as the reward for their labors.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
baehrens: PG De magistris et discipulis u01-rem-close
orientation: Evagrius is closing his treatise by comparing the monastic community's progress under its leader to Israel's journey through the desert toward the promised land.
